lessons.title: Comparing Things
goals: ⚖️ Compare two things: bigger, smaller, faster
warmup: ⚖️ Guess
Which is bigger: an elephant or a car? / Fil yoki mashina — qaysi katta?
🐘 Quick compare
Is a horse faster than a cow? / Ot sigirdan tezmi?

x: An elephant is bigger than a cat.
A mouse is smaller than a rabbit.
A car is faster than a bike.
A turtle is slower than a dog.
He is taller than his brother.
A phone is more expensive than a book.
My brother is older than me.
My sister is younger than me.

grammar.rule: Short adjectives: **-er + than** (big→bigger, fast→faster) · long: **more + adj + than** (more expensive)
ex: A bike is **faster than** a car? No — a car is **faster than** a bike.
This phone is **more expensive than** that one.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: A giraffe is ___ (tall) than a horse.
Winter is ___ (cold) than summer.
A plane is ___ (fast) than a train.
My bag is ___ (heavy) than yours.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: This film is ___ than that one. → a) more interesting b) interestinger c) most interesting

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: is / than / A / faster / car / a / bike / .
than / is / My / sister / younger / me / .

reading.title: Two Cities
reading.passage: Tashkent and Samarkand are two wonderful cities. Tashkent is bigger than Samarkand and it has more people. Samarkand is older — it is more than 2,700 years old! Tashkent is busier, with more cars and shops. Samarkand is quieter and more beautiful, with its blue domes. Food is cheaper in Samarkand. Both cities are beautiful in their own way.
qs: Which city is bigger?
Which city is older?
Where is food cheaper?
Which city is quieter?

listening.title: Which Is Better?
qs: Which city is bigger?
Which phone is cheaper?
Which bag is heavier?
listening.script: Listen. Tashkent is bigger than Fergana. This red phone costs three million som, but the blue phone is cheaper. This red bag is heavy, but the blue bag is heavier than the red one.

writing.title: Compare Two Things
writing.task: Write 4 comparisons: '... is bigger/faster/more expensive than ...' about your town or things you know.
writing.uz: Shahringiz yoki bilgan narsalar haqida 4 taqqoslash yozing.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: Which is bigger, your town or Tashkent?
Who is taller, you or your partner?

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Compare 3 things in your home and tell your family. / Uyda 3 ta narsani taqqoslang.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 comparison words 3× · Grammar: 6 comparative sentences · Reading: re-read 'Two Cities' · Speaking: compare your school and another school.
teacher: Use real classroom objects for comparison practice.
Drill -er spelling rules: big→bigger (double g), hot→hotter.
Watch for 'more big' — explain short vs long adjectives.
Compare people students know — always a hit.

lessons.title: Free Time Activities
goals: 🎨 Talk about hobbies and free time
Bo'sh vaqt va qiziqishlar haqida gapirish
🕐 Say how often you do things
warmup: 🎨 My hobby
What do you like to do in your free time? / Bo'sh vaqtingizda nima qilasiz?
🎮 Quick poll
Raise your hand if you like playing games! / O'yin o'ynashni yaxshi ko'rasizmi?

x: We ride our bikes on Sunday.
I listen to music every day.
I walk the dog every evening.
My father and I play chess.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: I like ___ (swim) in summer.
She loves ___ (listen) to music.
He enjoys ___ (play) chess.
We like ___ (watch) movies.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: I like ___ football. → a) play b) playing c) played

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: music / loves / She / listening / to / .
like / We / games / playing / .

reading.title: My Free Time
reading.passage: In my free time I like doing different things. I love reading comics and drawing pictures. On sunny days, I ride my bike with my cousin. I also enjoy playing chess with my father — but he always wins! In the evening, I like watching movies with my family. Sometimes we listen to music and sing together. What do you like doing in your free time?
qs: What does the writer love doing?
Who does he ride his bike with?
Why does he like playing chess?
What does the family do in the evening?

listening.title: What Do They Like?
qs: What does John like doing?
What does Lily love doing?
What does Tom enjoy doing?
listening.script: Listen. John likes riding his bike in the park. Lily loves reading comics and drawing. Tom enjoys playing football with his friends every weekend.

writing.title: My Hobbies
writing.task: Write 5 sentences about your free time activities using like/love/enjoy.
writing.uz: Bo'sh vaqt mashg'ulotlaringiz haqida 5 gap yozing.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask 3 people about their hobbies. Report their answers. / 3 kishidan qiziqishini so'rang.

quiz: Name 4 free time activities in English.
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 activities 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences with like/love/enjoy · Reading: re-read 'My Free Time' · Speaking: tell your family about your hobbies.
teacher: Survey the class about hobbies — make a chart.
Drill like/love/enjoy + -ing with pictures.
Watch for 'I like play' — echo correct form.
This connects to L53 (invitations to do activities).

lessons.title: Making Invitations
warmup: 📨 A party
Imagine a birthday party. Who will you invite? / Tug'ilgan kun — kimni taklif qilasiz?
🎉 Would you like...?
Teacher: 'Would you like to play a game?' / O'ynaysizmi?

x: I want to invite my friends.
We are having a party on Saturday.
Do you want to join us?

grammar.rule: Invitations: **Would you like to...? / Let's... / Do you want to...?** · Accept: Yes, I'd love to · Decline: I'm sorry, I can't
grammar.uz: Taklif: 'Would you like to...?', qabul: 'Yes, I'd love to'
ex: **Would you like to** come to my party?

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: Would you like ___ come to my party? (to/for)
Let's ___ chess. (play/playing)
I'm sorry, I ___ come. (can't/don't)
Are you ___ on Friday? (free/busy)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Invite a friend to a party: → a) Would you like to come? b) Go away c) You must come!

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: like / Would / to / come / you / ?
Let's / football / play / !

reading.title: The Invitation
reading.passage: 'Hi Aziz! Would you like to come to my birthday party on Saturday?' wrote Umid. Aziz smiled. 'Sure, I'd love to! What time?' 'At four o'clock,' Umid replied. 'But I'm sorry, my sister can't come — she is busy.' 'That's okay,' said Umid. 'Let's play football after the party!' Aziz agreed happily.
qs: When is the party?
What time does it start?
Why can't Umid's sister come?
What will they do after the party?

listening.title: The Phone Call
qs: Who is calling?
What does she invite him to?
Can the boy come? Why?
listening.script: Listen. 'Hello, this is Sara. Would you like to come to my house tomorrow? We're going to make pizza!' 'Sure, I'd love to!' 'Great! And would you like to invite your brother too?' 'I'm sorry, he can't — he has football practice.'

writing.title: Write an Invitation
writing.task: Write an invitation message to a friend: the event, the day, the time. Use 'Would you like to...?'.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: Would you like to come to my party?
Yes, I am. / Sorry, I'm busy.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Invite someone to an activity this week in English. / Bu hafta kimnidir inglizcha taklif qiling.

quiz: How do you accept? → 'Yes, ___ love to.'
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 invitation words 3× · Grammar: write an invitation + answer · Reading: re-read 'The Invitation' · Speaking: practice invitations with your family.
teacher: Act out invitations with real party props.
Drill the polite forms; watch for 'Would you like come'.
Teach both accept and decline — students need both.
This feeds L54 workshop.

lessons.title: Weekend Plans Workshop
goals: 📨 Invite friends to join the plan
🗣️ Present your plan to the class
warmup: 💡 Ideas
Name 5 weekend activities. / 5 ta dam olish mashg'uloti ayting.
📨 Invitation review
Quick drill: 'Would you like to...?' / Taklifni takrorlang.

x: We're going to have a picnic.
There is a concert on Sunday.

practice.title: Build a Weekend Plan
items: Choose a day: Saturday or Sunday. / Kun tanlang.
Choose 3 activities: picnic, museum, cinema, park, market... / 3 ta mashg'ulot tanlang.
Write times: 'At 10 we're going to...' / Vaqtlarni yozing.
Invite a partner: 'Would you like to join us?' / Juftingizni taklif qiling.
Present your plan to the class. / Rejani taqdim eting.

speaking.title: My Weekend Plan
speaking.body: Present your plan: 'On Saturday we're going to...' (5 sentences). / Rejangizni 5 gap bilan aytib bering.

speaking.title: Invite and Accept
speaking.body: Invite your partner to your plan. They accept or decline politely. / Juftingizni taklif qiling — u qabul qilsin yoki rad etsin.

speaking.title: Vote
speaking.body: Class votes for the best plan! / Sinf eng yaxshi rejaga ovoz bersin.

lessons.homework: Write your perfect weekend plan (5 sentences with going to) and practice presenting it. / Ideal dam olish rejangizni yozing.
teacher: Workshop: students plan in groups of 3.
Provide activity word banks and time phrases.
Encourage 'Would you like to join us?' in presentations.
Vote on the best plan — friendly competition.

lessons.title: Speaking Circle: My Free Time
goals: 🕐 Say how often you do things
warmup: 🎨 Hobby show
Mime your hobby — students guess! / Qiziqishingizni imo bilan ko'rsating.
🎮 Free-time words
Say 5 activities quickly. / 5 ta mashg'ulot ayting.

x: I usually play games after school.
I walk the dog every day.
I read in my free time.

practice.title: Free Time Discussion Cards
items: What is your favourite hobby? / Sevimli mashg'ulotingiz?
How often do you do it? / Qanchalik tez-tez qilasiz?
What do you do on Sundays? / Yakshanba kuni nima qilasiz?
Do you like watching movies? What kind? / Kino ko'rishni yoqtirasizmi?
Is there any hobby you want to try? / Qaysi mashg'ulotni sinab ko'rmoqchisiz?

speaking.title: My Free Time
speaking.body: Speak for 2 minutes about your free time: your favourite hobby, how often you do it, what you do at weekends. / Bo'sh vaqtingiz haqida 2 daqiqa gapiring.

speaking.title: Interview
table: How often do you play games?
Yes, I love it. / Not really.
What do you want to try?

speaking.title: Active Listening
speaking.body: Write 3 facts about your partner's free time. / Juftingiz haqida 3 fakt yozing.

lessons.homework: Write about your perfect free-time day (8-10 sentences). Practice speaking it. / Bo'sh vaqtingiz haqida yozing.
teacher: Speaking circle: focus on fluency, not accuracy.
Keep turns short; everyone speaks.
Use the interview table for pair work.
Note any frequent errors to review next lesson.

lessons.title: My Weekend
goals: 🌞 Narrate last weekend in the past
O'tgan dam olish kunini aytib berish
warmup: 🌞 Last weekend
Tell one thing you did last weekend. / O'tgan dam olishda nima qildingiz?
🔄 Past review
went, saw, had, ate, played — make sentences! / O'tgan zamon gaplari tuzing.

x: We had a barbecue in the garden.

grammar.rule: Weekend story: **regular + irregular past** verbs in time order
grammar.uz: Dam olish hikoyasi: o'tgan zamon fe'llari tartibda
ex: In the evening we **had** a barbecue.
On Sunday I **rested** and **watched** a film.
Yakshanba kuni dam oldim va film ko'rdim.
mistake: Wrong: *On Sunday I watch a film.*
Right: *On Sunday I watched a film.*

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: On Saturday I ___ (go) to the park.
We ___ (have) a nice time.
My father ___ (cook) a big dinner.
In the evening we ___ (watch) TV.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Last weekend we ___ to the mountains. → a) go b) went c) gone

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: Saturday / I / on / went / fishing / .
a / had / We / great / weekend / .

reading.title: A Perfect Weekend
reading.passage: Last weekend was perfect. On Saturday morning, my family and I went to the mountains. We walked for two hours and saw beautiful views. My father took many photos. In the evening we came home and had a barbecue in the garden. On Sunday, we visited my grandparents. My grandmother cooked my favourite food. I had a wonderful weekend!
qs: Where did the family go on Saturday?
How long did they walk?
What did they do in the evening?
Who did they visit on Sunday?

listening.title: The Weekend
qs: What did the girl do on Saturday?
Where did she go on Sunday?
What did she see there?
listening.script: Listen. On Saturday I went to the park with my friends. We played games and had ice cream. On Sunday I visited my grandmother. She showed me her garden. I saw many flowers and one funny cat!

writing.title: My Weekend Story
writing.task: Write your own weekend story (8-10 sentences) using past verbs in order.
writing.uz: Dam olish kuningiz haqida hikoya yozing.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What did you do on Saturday?
Did you have a good time?
What did you do on Sunday?

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: This weekend, collect 3 English sentences to share on Monday! / Shu dam olishda 3 gap yodlab keling.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 6 weekend words 3× · Grammar: 8-sentence weekend story · Reading: re-read 'A Perfect Weekend' · Speaking: tell your family about your last weekend.
teacher: Anchor lesson consolidating L41-42.
Model a weekend story, then students write their own.
Watch for tense mixing within one story.
Collect Monday stories — a great routine.

lessons.title: Adverbs of Frequency
warmup: 🔁 How often?
I drink tea every day — that's 'always'. What about you? / Qanchalik tez-tez choy ichasiz?
📅 Routine review
Name 3 things you do every day. / Har kuni qiladigan 3 ishingizni ayting.

x: Odatda soat 7 da kechki ovqat yeymiz.
I walk to school every day.
I never go to bed late.

grammar.rule: Frequency adverb goes **before the main verb** (I always do) but **after am/is/are** (I am always...)
grammar.uz: Ravish fe'ldan oldin, 'am/is/are' dan keyin keladi

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: I ___ eat breakfast. (always)
She is ___ on time. (always)
We ___ watch TV. (sometimes)
He ___ drinks coffee. (never)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Where do you put 'always'? → a) I always get up b) I get up always c) Always I get up

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: always / I / get / early / up / .
never / drinks / He / coffee / .

reading.title: My Morning Routine
reading.passage: I have a simple morning routine. I always get up at six o'clock and I am always on time for school. I usually have bread and tea for breakfast. I often walk to school with my friend. I sometimes listen to music on the way. I rarely miss a day. I never go to school without my books — that is my golden rule!
qs: What time does the writer get up?
What does he usually have for breakfast?
How does he go to school?
What is his golden rule?

listening.title: How Often?
qs: How often does Ali eat fast food?
How often does he walk?
What does he never do?
listening.script: Listen. Ali has healthy habits. He never eats fast food. He always walks to school. He usually drinks milk, not cola. He sometimes plays football on weekends — but he never plays on school nights!

writing.title: My Habits
writing.task: Write 5 sentences about your habits using: always, usually, often, sometimes, never.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: How often do you do homework?

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Observe your day and report: 'I always/never...' at dinner. / Kuningizni kuzating va ayting.

quiz: Fill: 'I ___ (never) eat candy in the morning.'
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 words 3× · Grammar: 6 habit sentences with frequency adverbs · Reading: re-read 'My Morning Routine' · Speaking: talk about habits with your family.
teacher: Draw the frequency ladder (100% → 0%).
Drill position: before main verb, after be.
Watch for 'always I' at the start of sentences.
Link to L58: build a typical week.

lessons.title: A Typical Week
goals: 📅 Use days of the week in context
warmup: 📅 Days drill
Say the days of the week fast! / Hafta kunlarini tez ayting.
🔁 Frequency review
always / usually / sometimes / never — what do you do? / Ravishlarni takrorlang.

x: On Monday I go to school.
The weekend is my favourite time.
We have five classes on Wednesday.
In my spare time I read.
I go to the cooking club on Fridays.
I do sports twice a week.
Haftada ikki marta sport bilan shug'ullanaman.

grammar.rule: Describe a week: **On + day** + activity + **frequency adverb**
ex: **On Monday I always** go to school.
Dushanba kuni har doim maktabga boraman.
**On Friday I sometimes** go to the club.
Dam olish kunlari odatda dam olaman.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: ___ Monday I go to school. (On/In)
I ___ do my homework. (always)
___ the weekend we rest. (At/On)
She ___ plays games. (sometimes)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: On Tuesday I ___ football. → a) always play b) play always c) always playing

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: Monday / on / school / to / I / go / .
sometimes / club / Friday / I / on / go / the / to / .

reading.title: Aziz's Week
reading.passage: Aziz has a busy but happy week. On Monday he goes to school and always does his homework. On Tuesday he plays football with his friends. On Wednesday he usually helps his mother in the kitchen. On Thursday he reads a book. On Friday he sometimes goes to the cooking club. At the weekend, he plays with his cousins and rests. A typical week for Aziz!
qs: What does Aziz always do on Monday?
What does he do on Tuesday?
Where does he go on Fridays?
What does he do at the weekend?

listening.title: A Typical Week
qs: What day does the girl go swimming?
What does she do on Wednesday?
What does she do at the weekend?
listening.script: Listen. My typical week: on Monday and Tuesday I go to school. On Wednesday I always go swimming. On Thursday I visit my grandmother. On Friday I sometimes meet my friends. At the weekend I help at home and rest.

writing.title: My Typical Week
writing.task: Write your week (7 sentences, one per day) using frequency adverbs.
writing.uz: Haftangiz haqida har kun uchun bittadan gap yozing.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What do you do on Mondays?
What do you do at the weekend?

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Tell your family about your typical week. Ask them about theirs. / Oilangizga haftangiz haqida aytib bering.

quiz: Fill: '___ Friday I go to the club.' (On/In)
Correct: 'In Monday I go to school.'
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 week words 3× · Grammar: 7-sentence typical week · Reading: re-read 'Aziz's Week' · Speaking: share your week with your family.
teacher: Build the week grid on the board together.
Drill 'On + day'; watch for 'In Monday'.
Let students compare their weeks in pairs.
This is real-life English — schedules matter.

lessons.title: Plan a Weekend Trip
goals: ⚖️ Compare places to choose the best
warmup: 🗺️ Travel words
Name 5 things you take on a trip. / Safarga nima olib borasiz?
💡 Where to?
Name 3 places to visit near your town. / Shahringiz yaqinida 3 joy ayting.

practice.title: Plan Your Trip
items: Choose a place: mountains, lake, big city, village. / Joy tanlang.
Choose transport: bus, car, train. / Transport tanlang.
Write 4 activities: 'We're going to swim / take photos...' / 4 ta mashg'ulot yozing.
Pack your backpack: list 5 items. / Ryukzakga nima olib borasiz?
Present your plan to the class. / Rejani taqdim eting.

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: going / to / We're / the / lake / go / to / .
going / take / I'm / to / photos / .

speaking.title: Present Your Trip
speaking.body: Present: where, how you're going, 4 activities. / Qayerga, qanday, nima qilasiz — taqdim eting.

speaking.title: Compare and Choose
speaking.body: Compare two trip ideas: 'The mountains are cooler than the city.' Which is better? / Ikki rejani taqqoslang.

speaking.title: Vote
speaking.body: Class votes for the best trip plan! / Sinf eng yaxshi rejaga ovoz bersin.

lessons.homework: Write your final trip plan (6 sentences with going to) and draw a small map. / Sayohat rejangizni yozing.
teacher: Workshop: plan in groups of 3.
Provide travel word bank and map pictures.
Encourage comparatives: 'the lake is closer than the mountains'.
Vote on the best plan to keep energy high.

lessons.title: Speaking Circle: Pre-Intermediate Review
goals: 🎯 Review L41-59: past, going to, comparatives, frequency
🗣️ Speak about past and future fluently
O'tmish va kelajak haqida ravon gapirish
👥 Use all tenses in one conversation
warmup: 🎯 Tenses quiz
go→went, do→did, eat→ate. Say the past! / O'tgan zamonni ayting.
🔄 Going to review
'I'm going to...' — what are your plans? / Rejalaringizni ayting.

practice.title: Review Stations
items: Past: 'Yesterday I went to...' — tell 3 things. / Kecha qilgan 3 ishingizni ayting.
Going to: 'Next weekend I'm going to...' — 3 plans. / Keyingi rejalaringiz.
Compare: '... is better than ...' — 2 comparisons. / 2 taqqoslash.
Frequency: 'I usually... / I never...' — 2 habits. / 2 odat.
Invite: 'Would you like to...?' — invite your partner. / Taklif qiling.

speaking.title: My Story
speaking.body: Speak for 2 minutes mixing past and future: what you did last weekend and what you're going to do next. / O'tgan va kelajak haqida gapiring.

speaking.title: Interview
table: What did you do last weekend?
What are you going to do tomorrow?
Who is taller, you or your friend?
How often do you play games?

speaking.title: Active Listening
speaking.body: Summarize your partner's story in 3 sentences. / Juftingizning hikoyasini 3 gapda ayting.

quiz: Say the past of: buy, make, come.
lessons.homework: Write your best story of the review (10 sentences: past + future). Practice speaking it. / Eng yaxshi hikoyangizni yozing.
teacher: Speaking circle consolidating L41-59.
Run review stations so every student speaks.
Note any weak areas for targeted review.
Celebrate progress — next band is Strong A2!
